subject: Request: 4-hour KV retention exception for FinReg Analytics
body:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@finreganalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@finreganalytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:43 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: data handling discussion — 4-hour window ask

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap from our side and the specific ask so your team can scope:

- FinReg is evaluating Redwood for our rules-engine assistant (sensitive PII regularly present).
- We need a data-handling guarantee that model inputs are not retained beyond operational needs.
- Proposed exception: KV cache and request logs retained no longer than 4 hours (rolling window) for the production environment.
- We understand this is outside your standard short-window pilot but wanted to start the conversation on feasibility, security controls, and any price/ops tradeoffs.

Can you confirm what evidence you’d share for SOC 2 coverage and whether a 4-hour retention carveout is something Redwood would consider for an enterprise pilot (and what constraints or premium applies)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call with legal/security if helpful.

Best,
Sophie Grant
Head of Product Security
FinReg Analytics

----
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@finreganalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling discussion — 4-hour window ask

Sophie — thanks for the clear summary. Appreciate you flagging the 4-hour window up front.

Short answers up front:
- We can explore a 4-hour KV/log retention carveout as a limited pilot under a defined scope.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a narrow contract carveout (DPA addendum) that both sides sign.
- There are operational constraints: shorter windows reduce our ability to serve high-throughput live requests from cache, and we may recommend a small burst buffer (ephemeral replicas) — we will outline tradeoffs below.

Next steps I propose:
1) Ben to propose a pilot plan and pricing for the 4-hour retention exception.
2) Marissa to coordinate DPA redline and provide SOC2 artifacts and a short ops runbook (what we can provide to FinReg).
3) Schedule a 30-min legal/security touchpoint if you want to run contract language in real time.

Ben / Marissa — looping you both in. Sophie — what days/times work for a quick follow-up this week?

—Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

----
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@finreganalytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling discussion — 4-hour window ask

Sophie / Jordan —

Appreciate the ask. A few concrete points from engineering and pricing we discussed internally:

Operational feasibility:
- We can implement a 4-hour rolling TTL on KV and request logs as a pilot. This requires enabling per-customer ephemeral cache partitions and disabling long-tail tracing for that tenant.
- Tradeoffs: a 4-hour TTL will increase per-token compute by ~8–12% due to less effective prefix caching and more frequent cache misses. Also increases IOPS on GPU nodes for short-lived KV churn.

Security & evidence:
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary (control mappings) and a redacted auditor report under NDA.
- We will produce an ops runbook and an architecture diagram for the ephemeral partitioning approach.

Contract & pricing:
- We typically reserve this level of retention customization for enterprise pilots with committed monthly minimums. For a 3-month pilot, proposed commercial terms: $30k/month commit + usage overage at standard rates. We can revisit price if pilot succeeds and scales.
- DPA addendum: we will accept a 4-hour TTL clause scoped to production traffic for the FinReg tenant only. All other Redwood telemetry (billing metrics, system health) will remain standard with anonymization where practicable.

Attachments attached: SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf (high level), DPA-redline-v3.docx (initial redline), redwood-4hr-kv-config-example.json (ops example).

Proposed immediate steps:
- Sophie: confirm you want to proceed with a 3-month pilot under the terms above.
- If yes, Marissa will pick up the DPA redlines and we’ll route for signature (DocuSign).
- Jordan will coordinate the engineering kickoff and a 60-min scoping call (we recommend including your security engineer).

Happy to discuss price/term flexibility — we want to make this low friction for your evaluation.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference

----
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@finreganalytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@finreganalytics.com
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling discussion — 4-hour window ask

Ben — thanks for the clear options and the artifacts. We’re aligned on the pilot approach, but two quick asks before we sign:

1) Can you provide the redacted SOC2 report under NDA? Procurement needs the auditor statement to move budget.
2) On the DPA addendum, we’ll propose one small wording change: the 4-hour TTL must apply to both KV cache and any request-level debug logs that may contain PII (we can share exact clause language).

Assuming those two items are OK, procurement will route the DocuSign this week and we’ll aim to start the pilot in the first week of January.

Sophie
Head of Product Security
FinReg Analytics

----
